Berbers.fact: The Taifa period ended when a Berber dynasty—the Moroccan Almoravids—took over al-Andalus; they were succeeded by the Almohad dynasty of Morocco, during which time al-Andalus flourished.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: One group of _____ seized Orihuela from its Berber garrison and took control of the entire region
Berbers.fact: After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms. One group of Saqaliba seized Orihuela from its Berber garrison and took control of the entire region.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: After the fall of Cordoba, the Zirids took over Granada in _____, forming the Zirid kingdom of Granada
Berbers.fact: After the fall of Cordoba in 1013, the Saqaliba fled from the city to secure their own fiefdoms. After the fall of Cordoba, the Zirids took over Granada in 1013, forming the Zirid kingdom of Granada.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in _____, but failed
Berbers.fact: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in 1018, but failed.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Khayran then executed Abd ar-_____ IV
Berbers.fact: The Saqaliba Khayran, with his own Umayyad figurehead Abd ar-Rahman IV al-Murtada, attempted to seize Granada from the Zirids in 1018, but failed. Khayran then executed Abd ar-Rahman IV.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: Khayran's son, Zuhayr, also made war on the Zirid kingdom of Granada, but was killed in _____
Berbers.fact: Khayran's son, Zuhayr, also made war on the Zirid kingdom of Granada, but was killed in 1038.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: In Cordoba, conflicts continued between the _____ rulers and those of the citizenry who saw themselves as Arab
Berbers.fact: In Cordoba, conflicts continued between the Berber rulers and those of the citizenry who saw themselves as Arab. After being installed as caliph with Berber support, Sulayman was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: After being installed as caliph with Berber support, _____ was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies
Berbers.fact: After being installed as caliph with Berber support, Sulayman was pressured into distributing southern provinces to his Berber allies.

Berbers.fact: In Cordoba, conflicts continued between the Berber rulers and those of the citizenry who saw themselves as Arab. The Sanhaja departed from Cordoba at this time.

Berbers.fact: The Zenata Berber Hammudids received the important districts of Ceuta and Algeciras.

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids claimed a family relation to the Idrisids, and thus traced their ancestry to the caliph Ali.

Berbers.fact: In 1016 they rebelled in Ceuta, claiming to be supporting the restoration of Hisham II.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: They took control of Málaga, then marched on _____, taking it and executing Sulayman and his family
Berbers.fact: They took control of Málaga, then marched on Cordoba, taking it and executing Sulayman and his family.

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids claimed a family relation to the Idrisids, and thus traced their ancestry to the caliph Ali. Ali ibn Hammud al-Nasir declared himself caliph, a position he held for two years.

Berbers.fact: For some years, Hammudids and Umayyads fought one another and the caliphate passed between them several times. Hammudids also fought among themselves.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The last Hammudid caliph reigned until 1027.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: The Hammudids were then expelled from _____, where there was still a great deal of anti-Berber sentiment
Berbers.fact: The Hammudids were then expelled from Cordoba, where there was still a great deal of anti-Berber sentiment.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: The Hammudids remained in Málaga until expelled by the Zirids in 1056.

Berbers.fact: The Zirids of Granada controlled Málaga until 1073, after which separate Zirid kings retained control over the taifas of Granada and Malaga until the Almoravid conquest.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: During the taifa period, the _____ dynasty, based in Badajoz, controlled a large territory centered on the Guadiana River valley
Berbers.fact: During the taifa period, the Aftasid dynasty, based in Badajoz, controlled a large territory centered on the Guadiana River valley. The area of Aftasid control was very large, stretching from the Sierra Morena and the taifas of Mértola and Silves in the south, to the Campo de Calatrava in the west, the Montes de Toledo in the northwest, and nearly as far as Oporto in the northeast.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: According to Bernard Reilly, during the taifa period genealogy continued to be an obsession of the upper classes in al-Andalus.

Berbers.fact: Most wanted to trace their lineage back to the Syrian and Yemeni Arabs who accompanied the invasion.

Berbers.fact: Malikite disciple Abd Allah ibn Yasin accepted the invitation.

Berbers.fact: Traveling to Morocco, he set up a military monastery or ribat where he trained a highly motivated and disciplined fighting force.

Berbers.fact: In 1054 and 1055, employing these specially trained forces, Almoravid leader Yahya ibn Umar defeated the Kingdom of Ghana and the Zenata Berber.

Berbers.fact: Forced to resolve a Sanhaja civil war, he left control of the Moroccan conquests to his brother, Yusuf ibn Tashfin.

Berbers.fact: In 1083, Yusuf ibn Tashufin conquered Ceuta.

Berbers.fact: In the same year, al-Mutamid, king of the Taifa of Seville, traveled to Morocco to appeal to Yusuf for help against King Alfonso VI of Castile. After the fall of Toledo to Alfonso VI in 1085, al-Mutamid appealed again to Yusuf.

Berbers.fact: After the fall of Toledo to Alfonso VI in 1085, al-Mutamid appealed again to Yusuf.

Berbers.fact: This time, financed by the taifa kings of Iberia, Yusuf crossed to al-Andalus and took direct personal control of Algeciras in 1086.

Berbers.fact: The most serious native revolt against colonial power in French Algeria since the time of Abd al-Qadir broke out in 1871 in the Kabylie and spread through much of Algeria. By April 1871, 250 tribes had risen, or nearly a third of Algeria's population.

Berbers.fact: In 1912, Morocco was divided into French and Spanish zones.

Berbers.fact: In July 1921, the Spanish army in northeastern Morocco, under Manuel Silvestre, were routed by the forces of Abd el-Krim, in what became known in Spain as the Disaster of Annual. The Spaniards may have lost up to 22,000 soldiers at Annual and in subsequent fighting.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages

Berbers.fact: Tamazight is now taught in Aurès since the march led by Salim Yezza in 2004.

Berbers.subject: Indian Languages
Berbers.question: While _____ism had its roots before the independence of these countries, it was limited to the Berber elite
Berbers.fact: As a result, most Berbers had to study and know Arabic, and had no opportunities until the twenty-first century to use their mother tongue at school or university. Berbers.fact: While Berberism had its roots before the independence of these countries, it was limited to the Berber elite. However, Berberism's distribution remains uneven.

Berbers.fact: Another escalation took place in May 2017.
